messages:
Jordan Park: Hi all, I'm trying to finish onboarding but Okta is blocking me. After I set my password I get 'Device approval required' and clicking enroll fails with 'This device is not allowed'. Using personal MacBook (Ventura). @Lina can you advise?

Lina (People Ops): Welcome Jordan! :wave: Are you on a company laptop? If not we usually apply a temporary SSO override for 48h. Give me your corporate email and I'll check.

Jordan Park: jordan.park@redwood.com. Not received 1Password invite either so can't see internal docs.

IT Bot: Alert: device_enroll_needed for jordan.park@redwood.com. Troubleshooting guide: https://help.redwood.com/okta-enroll

Priya: Sometimes Okta blocks personal devices if device trust is required. Lina, did the auto-lift run?

Lina (People Ops): Looks like autogenerated lift didn't attach. Reapplying now, should be active in ~3 minutes. Also re-sending 1Password invite.

Noah (IT): I triggered a manual directory sync and reissued the SSO invite at 1862409980. Jordan, try logging in after clearing cookies or using an incognito window.

Jordan Park: Tried incognito, got further. Okta asked to enroll a device; I chose 'I don't have a company device' -> 'Use security key' and set up a passkey from my phone. Enrollment accepted and I got 1Password invite. Thanks!

Maya (DevEx): If you need CLI access: run `eval $(op signin --account redwood)` after accepting the SSO invite. If you hit a redirect loop, clear cookies for okta. Stay in touch if anything else.

Jordan Park: One last Q: will some apps still require the company laptop? I got a 'device approval required' message for the internal dashboard earlier.

Lina (People Ops): The temporary override covers most apps but we keep a few sensitive apps restricted to managed devices. Your laptop shipping info will be emailed shortly; once it's enrolled the temporary lift is removed.

IT Bot: temporary_sso_override applied for jordan.park until 1862560000.

Jordan Park: All good now, thanks team!
